versions.label: Ἀκολουθίαι τῶν ἀνωνύμων (April 1738)
versions.tradition_or_use: Roman Greek editions for Greek-rite Catholics generally
versions.distinctness_basis: Existing canonical witness. Its title names the office of Holy Communion and the Liturgies of Chrysostom, Basil and the Presanctified, and adds Sunday Apostle and Gospel readings. The date alone does not make it a new version; its relation to the 1754 Euchologion is unestablished.
versions.unresolved: The offered 202-image witness ends its first pagination at printed p. 91 (provider PP97), followed by an unnumbered dismissal leaf at PP98, whereas BnF describes [2]-128-100 pages; the Sunday Apostle and Gospel readings named on the title were not located in the bounded inspection. Raes reports a nine-volume Roman reprint of Arcudius's Anthologion in 1738; whether this volume belongs to that set is unestablished. See the proposed update.

versions.label: Παρακλητικὴ σὺν Θεῷ ἁγίῳ (April 1738)
versions.tradition_or_use: Roman Greek editions for Greek-rite Catholics generally
versions.distinctness_basis: A complementary office volume: the Paraklitike supplies the Sunday and weekday propers of the eight tones. The title claims a new printing corrected from the old books.
versions.unresolved: No page images seen. The Rome and Propaganda Fide imprint is bracketed by the cataloguer. Relationship to the nine-volume 1738 Anthologion reprint reported by Raes is unestablished; local Catholic reception is not shown.

versions.unresolved: No page images seen. The Rome and Propaganda Fide imprint is bracketed by the cataloguer. Relationship to the nine-volume 1738 Anthologion reprint reported by Raes is unestablished; local Catholic reception is not shown.

versions.tradition_or_use: Roman Greek editions for Greek-rite Catholics generally
versions.distinctness_basis: Raes reports that the Holy See's commission for the Eastern books issued the Triodion in 1724 under a deliberately false Bologna imprint. It would be the earliest Roman Greek Catholic proper book in this repertoire.

versions.label: Εὐχολόγιον τὸ μέγα (Rome, 1754)
versions.tradition_or_use: Roman Greek editions for Greek-rite Catholics generally
versions.date_label: 1754 on the title; Ex quo primum dated 1 March 1756
versions.distinctness_basis: At the Marian intercession, the 1754 printing (printed p. 53) passes directly to the deacon's diptychs rubric, whereas the 1873 printing (pp. 65–66) prints a choir rubric with Ἄξιόν ἐστιν before it. This dates a printed-content difference, not the origin or first performance of the hymn.
versions.unresolved: No whole-book collation. The title image does not by itself prove the Propaganda press; that rests on the act and catalogues. See the proposed update.

versions.label: Μικρὸν Εὐχολόγιον σὺν Θεῷ ἁγίῳ (Rome: Polyglot Press, 1872)
versions.tradition_or_use: Roman Greek editions for Greek-rite Catholics generally
versions.distinctness_basis: A physically distinct small Euchologion opening with the order of the Divine Liturgy; its contents table (PDF page 186) lists the Chrysostom Liturgy only, not Basil or the Presanctified, and ends with Superiorum permissu. No substantive revision against 1754 or 1873 is established.
versions.unresolved: No whole-book collation has been made, and no graph ancestry is asserted.

versions.label: Εὐχολόγιον τὸ μέγα σὺν Θεῷ ἁγίῳ (Rome: Polyglot Press, 1873)
versions.tradition_or_use: Roman Greek editions for Greek-rite Catholics generally
versions.distinctness_basis: Same bounded difference as for 1754: the 1873 printing adds the choir rubric with Ἄξιόν ἐστιν and Τὴν τιμιωτέραν before the diptychs. A printing-state observation, not proof of a new anaphora.
versions.unresolved: The title prints Rome, the Polyglot Press and αωογʹ, but does not name Propaganda Fide. The handwritten number beside the library stamp reads 1501, a holding mark; the canonical passage's reading 1871 should be corrected (see limits). No whole-book collation.

versions.label: Ἱερατικόν (title: Rome, 1950; colophon: printed at Harissa, March 1952)

versions.date_label: 1950 on the title; printing finished March 1952 according to the colophon
versions.distinctness_basis: A celebrant book with Vespers, Orthros and the three Liturgies; the printed Holy See approval was seen on the image. It is not the Grottaferrata Horologion of 1950 and not an Athens Hieratikon. The title date (1950) and the colophon's completion of printing (March 1952, at the Melkite Paulist press in Harissa) are separate roles; the printing place is a relationship fact, not evidence of Melkite reception.
versions.unresolved: Modern editorial rights are not cleared. Exact substantive changes and reception by the Greek exarchates or Piana need primary evidence.
